status: DRAFT: not registered; no recorded run
recording: self-contained runtime gate (code/gate.py, a copy of experiments/2026-11-17-cpu-baselines/code/gate.py at eb2228b) and self-recorded manifests; not recorded by the team runtime
question: Does seeded range-bound pruning make the exact GPU range scorer faster on the full collection, and how much of any change comes from the range size, the work-list scheduling and the pruning itself?
hypothesis: Pruning scores far fewer postings and ranges (development census: at 64 seeds, median 64.6% / 41.7% / 21.8% of postings at range size 1024 / 512 / 256), so the pruned scorer is faster than the exhaustive control, more so at smaller ranges; per-query overhead (four extra launches, a 64-range seed phase) limits the gain
contract: GSP-CAP32-U32GUARDED-NUMERIC-TIES-v1; uint8 impacts, prepared integer query weights, uint32 accumulation under the conservative-bound guard, reported as uint64; ties by original numeric passage ID; all passages eligible
exactness: A range is skipped only when its bound (sum of query weight x largest impact of the term in the range x largest term multiplicity) is strictly below theta, the k-th best exact score among the seed ranges' documents. Every document of a skipped range scores at most its bound < theta, and k distinct seeded documents score >= theta, so no skipped document can be in the top k, ties included. Fewer than k seeded documents give theta = 0 and nothing is skipped

inputs.rule: checked by whole-file SHA-256 before any scoring
inputs.provenance: W512 and W256 built on cuda5 from the pinned GSP by range_bitpack_tool (`build GSP OUT SIZE positions`, uniform ranges), compiled from src/range_bitpack_tool.cpp and src/range_bitpack.h as last changed in 223cf4b; the same binary regenerated the pinned W1024 index with an equal hash

fixed.host: cuda5 (RTX 4070, UUID GPU-ab7b89ba-5664-fd05-e352-a4bc034e5ff7; host thread on CPU 0, local allocation)

implementations.v2: src/cuda_range_v2.cu unchanged (variant 5): one block per range, exhaustive
implementations.prune: src/cuda_range_prune.cu: five kernels per query (bounds, seed selection, seed scoring with theta, compaction, scoring of kept ranges with the final merge); scoring kernels are a persistent grid (occupancy x SMs blocks) over a work list; the per-range body is variant 5's. seeds 0 = the same path with nothing skipped
implementations.seed_count_choice: 64, fixed from the development census (work only, no timing): median postings within 3 percentage points of the oracle threshold's at every range size (2.9 / 2.2 / 1.9 at 1024 / 512 / 256), while 256 seeds gain at most 2.7 more

control: v2-w1024, the current best exact GPU scorer (full-collection median 0.686-0.690 ms in earlier sessions)
timing_boundary: Per query, host wall clock from building the query argument from its parsed (term, weight) pairs to the ordered top-k (original IDs and scores) in host memory, including every kernel launch, synchronisation and the result transfer (query_wall_ms, unchanged from v2). The pruned scorer's schedule statistics are copied after the boundary. Index loading, block maxima, tie ranks, the gate, output writes and checks are outside it

timing.order: every configuration once per pass, three passes with rotation offsets 0, ceil(n/3), ceil(2n/3)
timing.before_each_process: wait (60 s polls, at most 60 minutes) until no GPU compute process is listed and other users' CPU use over 5 s is at most CPU_LIMIT cores
timing.sampling: every 0.5 s during each process: nvidia-smi compute processes on the GPU and machine CPU time from /proc minus the scorer and the sampler; sampler on CPU 15
timing.eligibility: a timing process is ineligible if another GPU process was sampled during it (or its own was not), or other users' CPU use averaged more than CPU_LIMIT cores over its life; a process that exits non-zero while another GPU process was sampled is ineligible (contended failure); any other failure stops the run
timing.replacement: an ineligible process is kept under raw/ineligible/ and replaced; at most 3 replacements per configuration, a 4th stops the run
timing.cpu_limit_rationale: Every configuration is a GPU scorer with one host thread on CPU 0 (sampler on CPU 15, 14 other cores). The earlier GPU experiments (range batching, full-collection baselines) had no CPU rule. The CPU-baseline experiment's 1.0 core was first adopted here, but in dry-run dev-prune-01 another user's single-threaded job kept other CPU use at 1.1-2.7 cores for over 15 minutes with no GPU process, which would stall or fail the run without bearing on GPU timing. 4.0 cores is a quarter of the machine. It was set before registration and before any latency from this experiment was read; other users' CPU use is recorded for every process. The GPU rule (no other GPU process sampled) is unchanged

correctness_gate: From the timed source and binaries on the timed host: tests/check_range_bitpack.py for v2 and tests/check_range_prune.py for the pruned scorer (answers and the independent schedule model), two deliberate runtime-gate rejections (prune seed count, v2 score threads), every configuration once against the CPU reference with VERIFY=1 for the seeds-64 configurations (host recomputation of every answer and of the bounds, seeds, theta, scored ranges and postings), and every timing process's answers against the CPU reference. Any mismatch stops the run

analysis.primary: v2-w1024 / prune-w<size>-s64 for size 1024, 512 and 256: geometric mean over (process, query) pairs of median_control / median_pruned. All three are reported; none is selected after the fact
analysis.decomposition: v2-w1024 / v2-w<size> (range size, exhaustive); v2-w<size> / prune-w<size>-s0 (work-list scheduling); prune-w<size>-s0 / prune-w<size>-s64 (pruning)
analysis.descriptive: median, mean, p95, p99 of the query-process medians; scored range fraction and postings per query of each prune configuration (deterministic; checked identical across rounds and processes)
analysis.interval: crossed process/query bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 20261118, percentile 2.5/97.5; conditional on this session and the calibration queries

decision_rule: Pruning is adopted as the project's exact GPU scorer if a primary interval lies wholly above 1; the fastest such configuration by point estimate is named, with its decomposition. If no primary interval lies above 1, the result is reported as negative with the decomposition. The held-out evaluation would then need a separately frozen choice
limits: one host, one GPU (RTX 4070), k=10, batch 1
the seed count was set from calibration-query work counts, so the held-out evaluation is the unbiased test
pruning effectiveness depends on the document order (this index is BP-reordered) and on k
shared machine: absence of other processes in the samples does not prove exclusivity
calibration queries only; the 6,480 held-out queries are untouched
